title: Louis Armstrong, Oliver and Armstrong, and Sebastian's Cotton Club
summary: Garland says there was only one Louis, who learned from Oliver and went on his own, and recalls playing with Louis at Sebastian's Cotton Club.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: In New Orleans were there a lot of players that sounded as good as Louis Armstrong? Many of the people, you know New Orleans musicians say Louie was just one of many wonderful trumpet players.
There ain't no more Louie, there was only one and that's him.
Uh-huh. I see. So does he stand out above everyone else?
Louie holds up for himself,yeah. They all tried, lot of them right now, doing great trying to copy Louie, make all them high notes and things. I know a lot
of them guys messed up, split their lips all up. Trying to make all them high notes, you know. Louie look at them and laugh.
Did you hear Oliver and Armstrong play together?
How did Oliver do with young Louis? I mean, did he hold his own okay?
Oh, yeah, Oh, yeah, Oh, Louie watch Joe, you know, and listen to Joe and taking all his stuff, you know, and went off for himself.
Learning the way we spoke about it before?
And put his own ideas in there, you know.
That's right, that's right. That's great.
I played at the Cotton Club, where I used to play with Louie. Frank Sebastian's Cotton Club.
